claim: Human CT tests (WGCTA, CCTST) have weak subscale reliability: subscale alpha .17-.51 against totals of .68-.85, so only the total score is usable.
agent_test: Log only total pass/fail per check, not per-skill scores; test whether per-skill labels on S0 checks predict anything at equal tokens.

claim: CCTST total scores correlate strongly with SAT and verbal ability (r .44-.66), so CT tests mostly track general verbal ability; adding the CCTST to ACT and GPA changed adjusted R2 only from .392 to .393.
agent_test: Check whether our S0 gate score correlates with plain-model accuracy on the same item; if r is near 1 the gate adds nothing.

claim: Test-retest and pre-post change on the CCTST are small: Facione control classes gained +0.04 and +0.63 points (not significant); the whole-course gain was 0.74 of 34 points; test-retest r=.63.
agent_test: Use a no-intervention repeat run to set the noise floor before claiming any scaffold gain on a CT-style test.

claim: Instruction in critical thinking has a modest effect on tests (0.37 SD in 1990; continuous programs 0.47 vs periodic 0.15); a 2026 meta-analysis reports g=1.34 with I2=92%; the Huber-Kuncel and Abrami figures were only recalled, not verified. Reference scale added: Abrami 2015 g+=0.30 over 341 effects; Huber and Kuncel 2016 college gain about 50th to 72nd percentile (71 reports); CLA study 45% no significant 2-year gain.
agent_test: Compare scaffold gain with these effect sizes only after verifying b11 and b12; report gain in SD against the plain arm.

claim: Independent studies report lower validity than author-affiliated ones; WGCTA job-performance r .32-.52 is a corrected figure.
agent_test: Prefer independent, open item sets for the gate; avoid single-vendor tests.

claim: Test-taker attrition and motivation distort pre-post scores: the Thurgood Marshall WGCTA post-test median fell 9 points (59 to 50) with only 90 of 200 retested.
agent_test: Randomise item order and repeat runs to measure order and noise effects on the agent.

claim: Open-ended performance assessment is less reliable than multiple choice (CLA+ constructed response .43) and needs raters; G=.74 with 2 raters and .84 with 4.
agent_test: If we grade open answers with an LLM judge, use at least 2 independent judges and report agreement.

claim: LLM auto-scoring of CT essay subskills is only moderately reliable: best fine-tune accuracy .604, alpha .606; GPT-5 zero-shot .543; unseen subskills .39-.56.
agent_test: Do not rely on a single LLM judge for CT-quality logs; calibrate it against human codes on about 100 items.

claim: On Cognitive Reflection Test items, davinci-003 got 5% correct (80% lure), ChatGPT-3.5 59%, ChatGPT-4 96%, humans 38%; Binz and Schulz independently found GPT-3 wrong on all 3 classic CRT items.
agent_test: Run our agent and the plain model on 150 CRT items; modern models likely saturate, so use adversarially modified items.

claim: Cheap prompts move lure answers to correct ones on older models (algebra suffix 5% to 28%; 'check for invalid assumptions' 18% to 54%; few-shot 2% to 92%), but for ChatGPT-4 removing reasoning changed accuracy only 95% to 88%.
agent_test: Replicate at equal tokens: scaffold vs one-line instruction vs few-shot on CRT and semantic-illusion items with a current model.

claim: GPT-4 scored 163 on the LSAT (about 88th percentile) and contamination did not change it materially (-0.85% on the multiple-choice row, 25% of 40 items flagged).
agent_test: Use LSAT-style items from after the model cutoff as a clean gate benchmark.

claim: On LSAT logical and reading items GPT-4 beats the human average (LR 80.6, RC 85.9 vs 56), but on analytical reasoning (AR-LSAT constraint puzzles) it scores only 33-35% vs human 56-60%, and CoT does not help (34.4 vs 35.2). UPDATE 2025: reasoning models score far higher (GLoRE AR-LSAT: o1-mini 79.2, DeepSeek-R1 90.0, QwQ-32B 92.4 vs human 56, ceiling 91), so the AR-LSAT gap is gone for them; GLoRE's GPT-4 73.1 also differs from 33-43 elsewhere (prompt/set dependent).
agent_test: Test a solver-style operator (code or constraint check) on AR-LSAT items vs CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Neuro-symbolic solving improves AR-LSAT: Logic-LM with GPT-4 reached 43.04 vs 33.33 standard and 35.06 CoT; CoT averaged -3.2 on AR-LSAT.
agent_test: Add a code-based verification operator and compare with CoT on the 230 AR-LSAT items.

claim: Fine-tuned models exploit answer-option artefacts on logic datasets: ReClor RoBERTa 75.5% on EASY vs 40.0% on HARD; early LogiQA models 35% vs human 86%.
agent_test: Report scaffold results on the HARD split, not the whole set.

claim: GPT-4 API reaches 72.25% on LogiQA 2.0 and 87.20% on ReClor dev but drops on out-of-distribution items (LogiQA ood 48.21-58.49%); context carry-over matters (ood 9 vs 5 correct of 20).
agent_test: Keep each test item in a fresh context to avoid carry-over; test the scaffold on post-cutoff items.

claim: LLMs show human-like content effects: Wason with realistic rules is easier for GPT-3.5, PaLM 2-L, Chinchilla (z>2.2, p<.03) and humans; slow humans (>80 s) do better.
agent_test: Run abstract vs realistic version pairs; the scaffold should shrink the gap.

claim: Humans reading LLM answers detect planted errors poorly: P(correct) 0.245 for short wrong outputs, 0.542 medium, 0.307 long (N=24, modified Watson-Glaser items).
agent_test: Not an agent test; human verifiers are weak, so logs must be checkable by code.

claim: LLM use changes human CT: it helps under insufficient time but hurts under sufficient time (N=393); offloading profiles exist (N=353).
agent_test: Outside agent scope; flag only as a user-interaction risk.

claim: Zero-shot LLM classifiers are near random at fallacy detection on LOGIC; best language model 53.31 micro F1.
agent_test: Test a fallacy-checklist operator on the LOGIC set at equal tokens.

claim: Critical-questions prompting (CQoT) gives small gains on MT-Bench reasoning (Claude 3.5 Sonnet 8.6 to 8.95; GPT-4o 8.3 to 8.45); the full scheme beats steps 1+4 only. Checked: avg +4.61% reasoning, +5.4% math vs baseline/CoT, GPT-4o judge, no significance test, no equal-token control, not LSAT.
agent_test: Replicate against CoT at equal tokens on LSAT-LR and ReClor HARD.

claim: Dynamic tasks (iterative argumentation, belief revision) correlate only modestly with static CT tests (r .28-.33), with known-groups validity (debaters higher).
agent_test: Add a staged-evidence belief-revision task and measure update correctness.

claim: No published study tests Watson-Glaser, Cornell or CCTST on an LLM (Crossref and arXiv searches; coverage incomplete because other indexes were rate-limited). Second-pass searches (web, OpenAlex) again found none.
agent_test: Use open proxies (LSAT, LogiQA, ReClor, CRT) unless licence allows commercial items.

claim: Answer-position base rates and contamination inflate LLM benchmark scores (MMLU cloze base-rate effect; GPT-4 reports the lower decontaminated score).
agent_test: Randomise option order; use post-cutoff items.

claim: High LLM scores on human tests do not equal human-like ability: o1 scored 81.25% on Ennis-Weir (typical humans 37.5-62.5%), yet psychology students beat o1 on text-encoded Raven's.
agent_test: Use several tests, not one, in the gate.

claim: Reasoning models (2025) are near-saturated on ReClor and AR-LSAT and cluster at 78.7-81.4% on the 6,235-item LogiEval; only filtered subsets stay hard (LogiEval-Hard, 1,617 items, mean 37.97%).
agent_test: Use LogiEval-Hard or fresh post-cutoff items for the S0 gate; ReClor/AR-LSAT cannot show scaffold gains on current models.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human item difficulty does not predict LLM item difficulty (LogiEval Table 4, n=7 per band; models solve 18%-human items at 85.7% and miss 31%-human items); option count matters (5-option items 51.9-73.4% vs 4-choice 81-90%).
agent_test: Calibrate gate items on model pass rates; fix option count; shuffle options.

claim: Detecting a 3-point accuracy gain between two paired arms needs about 970 independent items (alpha .05, power 80%, paired variance 1/9); with 198 items the minimum detectable effect is 13.2% at K=1 and 7.5% at K=10 repeats; clustered items can inflate standard errors up to 3x.
agent_test: Plan N at least 1,000 paired items (cluster by passage); repeats alone cannot fix a small item set.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Temperature 0 is not deterministic: five LLMs on eight tasks varied up to 15% in accuracy across 10 identical runs (best-worst gap up to 70%); option reordering changes accuracy by tens of points under oracle ordering (GPT-4 Professional Law -30/+23).
agent_test: Report run-to-run spread of the plain arm, shuffle options, average over permutations.

claim: LLM judges match human-human agreement on chat preferences (GPT-4 85% vs human 81%) but show position bias (65% consistency) and are weak at fine-grained CT rubric levels (essay subskills alpha .606 best).
agent_test: Use position swap and reference answers for any LLM-graded critique; prefer closed-answer items.

claim: No evidence exists that dispositional scales (CCTDI, Need for Cognition) run on LLMs predict accuracy; LLM self-report scales are unstable under wording and option order, and persona prompts change bias rates but not shown to change accuracy.
agent_test: Do not build gates on disposition scales; any test would need option-order and wording controls.
